thesis: Coca-Cola is executing better than any staple in the market - Q1 2026 organic revenue +10%, comparable EPS +18%, operating margin up to 35%, guidance RAISED to +8-9% EPS growth, Coke Zero volumes +13% neutralizing the GLP-1 headwind, and a 64th consecutive dividend increase funded by $12.2B of guided FCF at a covered ~72% payout (the anti-PEP). The problem is arithmetic, not quality: at $83.78 (~30x FCF, 26x earnings, beta 0.35) the market discounts KO at roughly 6-7%; this framework's non-negotiable 10% hurdle prices the same cash flows far lower. KO is fully-valued excellence - the mirror-image lesson to PEP's uncovered-dividend trap.
catalysts: Q2 2026 results (~July 22, 2026); a fourth consecutive beat is the street's expectation
FY2026 comparable EPS growth guidance raised to +8-9% (off the $3.00 2025 base) - delivery
Coke Zero Sugar momentum (+13% volume) and protein/zero portfolio expansion into GLP-1-era demand
Emerging-market volume growth on affordability packs
risk_factors: Valuation vs hurdle: ~30x FCF for mid-single-digit terminal growth fails a 10% discount rate by construction - the position only works if the market's ~6.5% required return persists
GLP-1 structural headwind: semaglutide patent expiries and oral forms in 2026 massively expand usage; full-sugar volumes are the exposed base
Net debt (~$25B order of magnitude) modestly levers the balance sheet
Currency and EM volatility on a majority-international revenue base
Any organic-growth normalization from 10% toward the historical 4-6% compresses the premium multiple

q1_2026_results.note: +12% reported, +10% organic; EPS 0.91 +18%, comparable 0.86 +18%; operating margin 35.0% vs 32.9%

fy2026_fcf_guidance.note: funds 64th consecutive dividend increase (~72% payout - covered); $5.2B buyback remaining
